scenes.tts: Cut a nerve in your arm, and its axons can grow back. Injure your spinal cord, and they mostly do not. Why?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Cut, Two Fates. An arm nerve and a spinal cord side by side; a cut appears in each.
scenes.narration: Cut a nerve in your arm, and its axons can grow back. Injure your spinal cord, and they mostly do not. Why?

scenes.tts: A cut splits each axon in two, and the two pieces have different fates.
scenes.visual: A long neuron, cell body at left, axon running to a muscle. A cut appears; the two pieces take different colours.
scenes.narration: A cut splits each axon in two, and the two pieces have different fates.

scenes.tts: The piece cut off from its cell body breaks down, in a limb nerve and in the spinal cord alike.
scenes.visual: The far piece is labelled distal, cut off. Icons: limb nerve and spinal cord, both ticked.
scenes.narration: The piece cut off from its cell body breaks down, in a limb nerve and in the spinal cord alike.

scenes.tts: The attached piece can grow a new tip, depending on the neuron and on what surrounds it.
scenes.visual: The near piece is labelled proximal, attached. A growth cone at its tip, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: The attached piece can grow a new tip, depending on the neuron and on what surrounds it.

scenes.tts: In a mouse nerve, the cut-off piece looks normal for a day and a half to two days. Then it falls apart.
scenes.visual: A timeline builds. First segment: 1.5 to 2 days, mouse sciatic nerve; then the distal piece fragments.
scenes.narration: In a mouse nerve, the cut-off piece looks normal for a day and a half to two days. Then it falls apart.

scenes.tts: Its debris is cleared quickly in a nerve, and slowly in the brain and cord.
scenes.visual: A second band starts while the first ends, overlapping it: debris clearing. Two rows: nerve, fast; brain and cord, slow and incomplete.
scenes.narration: Its debris is cleared quickly in a nerve, and slowly in the brain and cord.

scenes.tts: Meanwhile, after a delay, the attached piece may regrow. In people that is often about a millimetre a day. Or it stalls, as many central axons do.
scenes.visual: A third band starts after a delay and overlaps the clearing band: regrowth, lasting weeks to months. A tip advances along a ruler marked often about 1 mm a day, depending on the nerve; a second tip stops.
scenes.narration: Meanwhile, after a delay, the attached piece may regrow. In people that is often about a millimetre a day. Or it stalls, as many central axons do.

scenes.tts: A sensory neuron in a spinal ganglion offers a test. It has one nucleus and two branches.
scenes.visual: A dorsal root ganglion neuron: one branch out into a peripheral nerve, one into the spinal cord.
scenes.narration: A sensory neuron in a spinal ganglion offers a test. It has one nucleus and two branches.

scenes.tts: Injure each branch, in separate experiments. Which one regrows?
scenes.visual: Two matched ganglion neurons side by side. In the first, only the peripheral branch is cut. In the second, only the central branch, inside the spinal cord, is injured. A question mark over each.
scenes.narration: Injure each branch, in separate experiments. Which one regrows?

scenes.tts: The branch in the nerve regrows. The branch in the cord mostly does not. Same kind of neuron, different outcome. Is it the tissue, or what each injury tells the cell body?
scenes.visual: The peripheral branch regrows; the central branch stays stubby. Label: same neuron type, different outcome. Two candidate labels: the tissue? the signal to the cell body?
scenes.narration: The branch in the nerve regrows. The branch in the cord mostly does not. Same kind of neuron, different outcome. Is it the tissue, or what each injury tells the cell body?

scenes.tts: Test the second. Cut the nerve branch first, and the cord branch regrows better later. This is the conditioning lesion. So the neuron's own state matters, and the tissue may too.
scenes.visual: A separate sequence on one neuron: the peripheral branch is cut first; the central branch, injured later inside the cord, grows further. Label: conditioning lesion.
scenes.narration: Test the second. Cut the nerve branch first, and the cord branch regrows better later. This is the conditioning lesion. So the neuron's own state matters, and the tissue may too.

scenes.tts: So here is the one idea. One cut, two fates. The cut-off piece destroys itself, by a program it carries.
scenes.visual: On screen, line one: the cut-off piece destroys itself by a program it carries.
scenes.narration: So here is the one idea. One cut, two fates. The cut-off piece destroys itself, by a program it carries.

scenes.tts: The attached piece tends to regrow where the neuron's drive to grow outweighs the resistance of the tissue around it.
scenes.visual: Line two: the attached piece tends to regrow where drive outweighs resistance. Small label: a rule of thumb, not a measured quantity. A balance tips toward drive.
scenes.narration: The attached piece tends to regrow where the neuron's drive to grow outweighs the resistance of the tissue around it.

scenes.tts: So ask two things of any cut. What does the cut-off piece do? And at the attached piece, which side wins?
scenes.visual: Closing card: the cut-off piece, a program; the attached piece, drive against resistance.
scenes.narration: So ask two things of any cut. What does the cut-off piece do? And at the attached piece, which side wins?
